primary.key: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.
primary.s: Having named desire as the foe that drives a man to sin, Krishna, near the chapter’s close, ranks the powers within; Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 3.42, reads the closing ‘He’ as the Self, the witness of reason, and Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 3.42, as desire, strongest and most overpowering of all.
primary.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 3.42, tr. A. Mahadeva Sastri (1901); Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 3.42, tr. A. Govindacharya (1898); both archive.org

basis.words: He, the Self, the witness of reason, is superior to reason. … Supposing the senses and all, duddhi inclusive, were quiet and passive, desire or lust, which is craving, deeply rooted in the heart, and rajzas-born, will yet assert mastery … That which then is the most strong and overpowering, vis., kama (lust, desire, craving, or appetite for phenomenal experiences) is denoted by the pronoun ‘sah.’
basis.gloss: Śaṅkara on 3.42: the one beyond reason is the Self, the witness of reason. Rāmānuja on 3.42: even were the senses, mind and intellect (buddhi) quiet, desire, rooted in the heart and born of rajas, would still assert mastery; the pronoun ‘sah’ (he) denotes this strongest, most overpowering thing, desire (kāma). His 3.43 follows it through: knowing this desire that surpasses buddhi, destroy it. Operator note: packet.js prints Śaṅkara’s words above, but recheck-evidence.js’s tag stripper (/<[^>]+>/) removes the packet text from Śaṅkara’s stray “<f Wherefore” (his 3.1 introduction) to Rāmānuja’s “go to work. >” (3.9), so every Śaṅkara piece on chapter 3 will read NOT FOUND by machine although it is printed there.

standby.key: As a flame is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as an embryo is wrapped by the amnion, so This is enveloped by it.
standby.s: Having named desire as the foe that drives a man to sin, Krishna pictures its hold in three likenesses; Madhva (Dvaita), on 3.38, reads them first as three grades of souls, the highest somewhat beset by desire, the middling much obscured, the lowest overwhelmed.
standby.src: Madhva, commentary on the Gita, 3.38, tr. S. Subba Rau (1906), archive.org india.history.resource.91865

basis.words: Just as flame is surrounded by smoke, so … the highest class of souls, is somewhat beset by desire, Just as a mirror may be covered with dust, so … the middling class is much obscured by desire. And just as the embryo is completely wrapped up in amnion, so … the lowest class, is overwhelmed by desire and lostin it. Thus ofall the three classes of Jivas, Desire more or less obstructs the knowledge
basis.gloss: Madhva on 3.38 (Subba Rau’s “V.” paragraph after verse 38): as smoke surrounds a flame, desire somewhat besets the highest class of souls; as dust covers a mirror, it much obscures the middling class; as the amnion wraps the embryo, it overwhelms the lowest, who are lost in it; so in all three classes of souls (jīvas) desire obstructs knowledge in degree. The ellipses skip only OCR noise standing for ‘this’. He then gives a second reading (the Lord, the mind, the soul), hence ‘first’ in the sentence.
